paragraphs: We are a leading post-acute healthcare company primarily focused on delivering high-quality skilled nursing care through a portfolio of independently operated facilities. Founded in 2013, we are one of the largest skilled nursing providers in the United States based on number of facilities. We also provide senior care, assisted living, and independent living options in some of our communities. In total, we operate 321 post-acute care facilities across 17 states serving over 31,700 patients daily. Our significant historical growth has been primarily driven by our expertise in acquiring underperforming long-term custodial care skilled nursing facilities and transforming them into higher acuity, high value-add short-term transitional care skilled nursing facilities. We believe our success is driven in significant part by our locally led, centrally supported operating model, through which we empower local leaders at each facility to operate their facility autonomously and deliver excellence in clinical quality and a superior experience for our patients. We provide our independently operated facilities with a comprehensive suite of technology, support, and back-office services that enable local leadership teams to focus more of their time and effort on providing quality care to patients. We believe our operating model delivers value to all of our healthcare stakeholders, including patients and families, referring providers, payors, and administrators and clinicians.

The post-acute care ecosystem serves individuals who need additional help recuperating from acute conditions, illnesses, or serious medical procedures after they have been discharged from the hospital. This ecosystem ranges from higher acuity, higher-cost settings, such as long-term acute care hospitals and inpatient rehabilitation facilities, to lower acuity, lower-cost settings, such as assisted living facilities, and home health. Skilled nursing facilities (SNFs) are positioned at the center of this ecosystem and play an essential role in providing cost efficient facility-based care to patients that have been discharged from hospitals but still require 24-hour in-patient services. SNFs can provide both long-term custodial care and higher value short-term transitional care. The SNF industry is large and growing, with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) expecting total industry expenditures to increase from $193.6 billion in 2022 to $283.3 billion in 2031, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.3%. Based on the number of facilities as reported by CMS, we are one of the largest SNF operators in the United States. We are primarily focused on providing higher value short-term transitional care and believe we are uniquely positioned to capitalize on the current underlying trends within the SNF industry and to capture a growing portion of the expected demand.

We believe that healthcare is local and we operate through a locally led, centrally supported model, recognizing that each patient, facility, and community is unique. To that end, we believe that our local leaders and their teams understand the distinct needs and priorities of their patients, staff, and facilities and are best positioned to make clinical and operational decisions in order to optimize patient outcomes and experience. To facilitate this, each of our facilities operates independently, led by a facility administrator and his or her interdisciplinary team of medical directors, nurses, therapists, specialty consultants, and operators. To assist these local teams in achieving their best clinical and operating potential, we provide each facility with access to PACS Services, and they are subject to the PACS Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (which is described elsewhere in this report) and a variety of other policies and procedures designed to help ensure our operations are conducted consistent with applicable law and prudent business practices. PACS Services is a comprehensive suite of offerings, including accounting, finance, human resources, payroll, accounts receivable and payable, legal, compliance, and risk management services, as well as a robust suite of technology tools. We operate in a highly regulated industry with stringent regulatory compliance obligations, which require robust regulatory compliance operations. Failure to operate in compliance with applicable laws and regulations could require significant expenditures and result in regulatory deficiencies and other regulatory penalties. PACS Services functions to support our regulatory compliance obligations across our organization, including through controlled billing and cost reporting practices and legal, risk management, and compliance support. PACS Services also provides teams of regional professionals available as resources to each facility, including a regional vice president (RVP) for each operational region, and regional clinical and non-clinical directors and consultants. We developed PACS Services to be a resource to help reduce administrative burden so that local leadership teams can focus on making decisions that improve the care, well-being, and quality of life of their patients.

We believe that talented local leadership is critical to the success of our model of independently operated, centrally supported facilities. At the facility level, administrators are effectively the chief executive officers, and together with other local licensed professionals, are ultimately responsible for the day-to-day operations of their respective facilities. We seek to recruit, train, and reward dynamic administrators for our facilities, and rely on them to work with their interdisciplinary

teams to implement policies and procedures that are appropriate and effective and result in positive outcomes. We support the delivery of excellent care by building excellent teams. We believe our model attracts high caliber, entrepreneurial professionals who value having considerable autonomy, accountability, and aligned incentives. We provide these professionals with leadership and industry training, guidance, and operational support. Our model is intended to align local leaders' incentives with facility and organizational success, encouraging them to dedicate themselves to the long-term future of their facilities. To create such alignment, we have developed an administrator compensation structure that prioritizes operational and financial performance, as well as quality of care. Our administrators understand that a well-performing facility is the result of providing quality care in an environment of healing and caring, and one that is appropriately staffed, supplied, and equipped to meet the needs of its patients. This dedicated focus by our administrators and their local teams on patient outcomes drives demand for our services and can ultimately result in higher patient census and profitability. We also seek to provide opportunities for upward career mobility, with many of our administrators being promoted from within our company to roles of increasing levels of responsibility. Our culture of meritocracy and pride of ownership has helped us retain experienced facility administrators as well as RVPs who had an average industry experience of 12.9 years as of December 31, 2025.

Excellence in clinical quality and experience for our patients is at the forefront of our mission. We believe our focus on quality is reflected in our CMS Quality Measures (QM) Star rating, occupancy rate, and skilled mix by nursing patient days (which refers to the number of days our Medicare and managed care patients receive skilled nursing services at SNFs as a percentage of the total number of days that patients from all payor sources receive skilled nursing services at SNFs for any given period). The QM Star rating is a number between 1 and 5 that is assigned to SNFs that participate in Medicare or Medicaid, and is based on an aggregate score across a range of quality reporting program requirements. As of December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, our average QM Star rating across our Mature facilities, which we define as facilities purchased more than 36 months prior to the measurement date, was 4.4, 4.3 and 4.2 Stars, respectively, compared to the industry average of 3.5, 3.4 and 3.6 Stars, respectively. For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, our average occupancy rate across our Mature facilities was 95%, 94%, and 93%, respectively, compared to the industry average of 79%, 77% and 76%, respectively. For the year ended December 31, 2025, our skilled mix by nursing patient days was 29%, as defined in Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.

We have historically grown primarily through our disciplined and balanced acquisition strategy. We generally aim to create value by identifying and acquiring underperforming custodial care focused facilities and converting them into higher-value short-term transitional care focused facilities by investing in clinical teams and processes and upgrading technology, equipment, training, staffing, aesthetics, and other aspects of the business. The resources and guidance offered by PACS Services are key to rapid integration of new facilities and provides our local leadership teams with an effective technology infrastructure, support tools, and regional support teams that enable local leadership to focus on operational improvements. Our facilities generally undergo an up to three-year post-acquisition transition period. During this period, we seek to implement best practices designed to realize and sustain the facility's full potential. These practices often result in significant improvements to clinical quality and other operational metrics, including skilled mix, occupancy rates and payor contracting. We believe the results of our acquisition strategy are demonstrated by our high average QM Star rating and occupancy rate for Mature facilities of 4.4 and 95%, respectively, as of December 31, 2025. As of December 31, 2025, the average QM Star rating and occupancy rate for New facilities, which we define as facilities purchased less than 18 months prior to the measurement date, was 3.5 and 81%, respectively.

Our portfolio of owned and leased properties is strategically located in 17 states: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Kansas, Kentucky, Missouri, Montana, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Washington. We anticipate that available acquisition opportunities will enable us to further penetrate our reach into these 17 states and to enter new states in the future. We believe our current markets are attractive and that the states in which we operate each has unique benefits, such as favorable reimbursement dynamics, high barriers to entry, or population growth of adults aged 65 and older, which is our primary patient demographic. We generally look for similar attributes in new markets that we enter. As of December 31, 2025 we leased 219 facilities, directly owned the real estate at 53 facilities, and owned partial interests in an additional 49 facilities through partnerships managed by third parties. As we continue to grow, we intend to explore additional purchases of real-estate assets, through purchase options or rights-of-first refusal in existing leases, as well as acquisitions and de novo construction of purpose-built facilities.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we generated total revenue of $5.3 billion, representing a CAGR of 30.4% over the last three years. A substantial portion of our revenue is generated from payments from third-party payors, including Medicare and Medicaid, which represent our largest sources of revenue and accounted for 33.7% and 40.5% of our routine revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025, respectively. For the year ended December 31, 2024, we
generated total revenue of $4.1 billion, and Medicare and Medicaid accounted for 33.8% and 40.4% of our routine revenue, respectively.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, our total operating expenses were $5.0 billion. For the same period, we generated net income of $191.5 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $505.0 million. For the year ended December 31, 2024, our total operating expenses were $4.0 billion and we generated net income of $55.3 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $279.5 million. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure. See the section titled "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations—Key Skilled Services Metrics and Non-GAAP Financial Measures—Non-GAAP Financial Measures" for a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.
As of December 31, 2025, we had total long-term liabilities of $3.6 billion.

Our locally led, centrally supported model is informed by our beliefs that "healthcare is local" and that each patient, facility and community is unique. Our administrators have significant autonomy in the decision-making process, subject to adherence to company policies and procedures, because we believe they know what is best for their community and their markets. Our 321 post-acute facilities are independently operated by interdisciplinary teams with robust administrative and consulting support from PACS Services.

We strive to have each of our facilities led by experienced and highly qualified administrators, who serves in effect as a "local CEO," alongside an interdisciplinary team of medical directors, clinicians, specialty consultants, and operators. In addition to a full clinical team of certified nursing assistants (CNAs), licensed practical nurses (LPNs), registered nurses (RNs), directors of nursing (DONs), and clinical directors, each facility has a local team of non-clinical staff including supervisors, admissions professionals, marketing professionals, and other business support personnel who have the common goal of providing excellent care and superior experiences for patients.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
Increased competition for, or a shortage of, nurses, nurse assistants and other skilled personnel could increase our staffing and labor costs and subject us to monetary fines.
If we fail to attract patients and residents and to compete effectively with other healthcare providers, our revenue and profitability may decline and we may incur losses.
Our business may be affected by the evolving regulatory framework for AI Technologies.
We rely significantly on information technology, and any failure, inadequacy or interruption of that technology could harm our ability to effectively operate our business.
We may not be able to successfully integrate acquired facilities and properties into our operations, and we may not achieve the benefits we expect from any of our facility acquisitions.
We may have difficulty completing partnerships that increase our capacity consistent with our growth strategy.
If we do not achieve or maintain competitive quality of care ratings from CMS or private organizations engaged in similar rating activities, our business may be negatively affected.
If we are unable to obtain insurance, or if insurance becomes more costly for us to obtain, our business may be adversely affected.
paragraphs: Our business involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider each of the following risk factors and all other information set forth in this report and our other filings with the SEC. Based on the information currently known to us, we believe that the following information identifies the most significant risk factors affecting our company. In addition, past financial performance may not be a reliable indicator of future performance and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods.

If any of the following risks and uncertainties develops into actual events or circumstances, they could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. You should carefully read the following risk factors, together with our combined/consolidated financial statements and the related notes and all other information included in this report and our other filings with the SEC. This report contains forward-looking statements that contain risks and uncertainties.

We depend upon reimbursement from third‑party payors, and our revenue, financial condition and results of operations could be negatively impacted by any changes in the acuity mix of patients in our facilities as well as changes in payor mix and payment methodologies and new cost containment initiatives by third-party payors.

Our revenue is affected by the percentage of the patients of our operating subsidiaries who require a high level of skilled nursing and rehabilitative care, whom we refer to as high acuity patients or skilled patients, and by our mix of payment sources. Changes in the acuity level of patients we attract, as well as our payor mix among Medicaid, Medicare, private payors and managed care companies, significantly affect our revenue. Changes to federal law affecting Medicaid funding and availability, including the enactment of the OBBBA, may materially affect our business and the operations of our independent subsidiaries. Because high acuity patients require more skilled nursing services and a higher level of care, we generally receive higher reimbursement rates for providing care to them. Lower acuity patients, who are typically Medicaid beneficiaries, typically require fewer skilled nursing services and thus we are typically paid lower rates by Medicaid for caring for them, sometimes at rates that do not cover our costs of providing care to the patient. Reimbursement rates provided for caring for skilled patients are more likely to meet or exceed the costs of providing care to those patients, thus enabling the facility to be fiscally sustainable. Given the generally predetermined nature of the reimbursement rates that we are paid for caring for patients, depending on their acuity level, if our labor or other operating costs increase disproportionately compared to the reimbursement rates we are paid for providing services, particularly with Medicaid patients, we will generally be unable to recover the increased costs from payors unless and until reimbursement rates are adjusted, and even then they may not be adjusted in full, in a timely manner, and are typically only adjusted on a prospective basis. Accordingly, if we fail to maintain our proportion of high acuity patients or if there is any significant increase in the percentage of the patients of our operating subsidiaries for whom we receive Medicaid reimbursement, it could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Initiatives undertaken by major insurers and managed care companies, including companies who run plans commonly referred to as Managed-Medicare and Managed-Medicaid, to reduce their costs and the amounts they pay providers may adversely affect our business. These tactics include contracting with healthcare providers to obtain services on a discounted basis. We believe that this trend will continue and may limit reimbursements for healthcare services. If insurers or managed care companies from whom we receive substantial payments were to reduce the amounts they pay for services and we did not wish to accept such reductions, we may lose patients if we choose not to renew our contracts with these insurers at their lower offered rates. Additionally, some payors have used the federal "No Surprises Act" or similar state legislation as a means to initiate re‑negotiation of reimbursement rates for providers and facilities, leading to litigation between these providers and/or facilities against payors and it may adversely affect us as well. In addition, sustained unfavorable economic conditions may affect the number of patients enrolled in managed care programs and the profitability of managed care companies, which could result in reduced payment rates.

We may not be fully reimbursed for all services for which each facility bills through consolidated billing or bundled payments, which could have an adverse effect on our revenue, financial condition and results of operations.

As previously disclosed on our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 as filed with the SEC on November 19, 2025, we identified material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting where we did not design and maintain sufficient processes to identify, assess, and communicate relevant risks to appropriate levels of the organization, including potential compliance issues received through the hotline process and we did not design and maintain adequate controls within the revenue process to appropriately recognize revenue for new services in accordance with Financial Accounting Standards Board Accounting Standards Codification Topic 606, Revenue from Contracts With Customers.

In addition, in connection with the preparation of our combined/consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, our management identified control deficiencies that, individually or in the aggregate, constitute material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting. The material weaknesses identified by management were that we did not design and maintain effective controls within the revenue process to address the completeness and accuracy of underlying data used to determine routine revenue. We also did not design controls to timely assess operational trends that could materially impact variable consideration estimates related to revenue recognition.

In addition, our Chief Executive Officer and our Interim Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, due to the material weaknesses, our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective, as such term is defined under Rules 13a-15(e) and 15(d)-15(e) under the Exchange Act, as of December 31, 2025. Management is committed to maintaining a strong internal control environment. In response to the identified material weaknesses above, management, with the oversight of the Audit Committee, is taking comprehensive actions to remediate the above material weaknesses. For additional information regarding the material weaknesses and our steps for remediation, please see "Part II, Item 9A, Controls and Procedures."

Considering the material weaknesses described above, management performed additional analysis and other procedures to ensure that our combined/consolidated financial statements were prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP). Accordingly, management believes that the combined/consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K fairly present, in all material respects, our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows as of and for the periods presented, in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

We use the following key skilled services metrics and non-GAAP financial measures to help us evaluate our business, identify trends that affect our financial performance, and make strategic decisions.

We monitor the below key skilled services metrics across all of our facilities and by Mature facilities, Ramping facilities, and New facilities. Mature facilities are defined as facilities purchased more than 36 months prior to a respective measurement date. Ramping facilities are defined as facilities purchased within 18 to 36 months prior to a respective measurement date. New facilities are defined as facilities purchased, or built, less than 18 months prior to a respective measurement date.

•Skilled nursing services revenue — Skilled nursing services revenue reflects the portion of patient and resident service revenue generated from all patients in skilled nursing facilities, excluding revenue generated from our assisted and independent living services.

•Skilled mix — We measure both revenue and nursing patient days by payor. Medicare and managed care patients, whom we refer to as high acuity patients, typically require a higher level of skilled nursing care. As a result, Medicare and managed care reimbursement rates are typically higher than those from other payors. In most states, Medicaid reimbursement rates are generally the lowest of all payor types. Changes in the payor mix can significantly affect our revenue and profitability. To monitor this performance, we evaluate two different measures of skilled mix:

◦Skilled mix by revenue — Skilled mix by revenue represents the portion of routine revenue generated from treating high acuity Medicare and managed care patients. Routine revenue refers to skilled nursing services revenue generated by contracted daily rates charged for skilled nursing services. Services provided outside of routine contractual agreements are recorded separately as ancillary revenue, including Medicare Part B therapy services, and are not routine revenue. The inclusion of therapy and other ancillary treatments in the contracted daily rate varies by payor source and by contract. Revenue associated with calculating skilled mix is based on contractually agreed-upon amounts or rates, excluding the estimates of variable consideration under the revenue recognition standard, Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) Topic 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (ASC 606).

◦Skilled mix by nursing patient days — Skilled mix by nursing patient days represents the number of days our high acuity Medicare and managed care patients receive skilled nursing services at skilled nursing facilities as a percentage of the total number of days that patients from all payor sources receive skilled nursing services at skilled nursing facilities for any given period.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家領導的後急性照護公司，主要專注於透過一組獨立運作的設施，提供高品質的專業護理服務。成立於2013年，我們是美國根據設施數量而言最大的專業護理服務提供者之一。我們也提供長者照護、輔助生活及獨立生活選項，於部分社區中。總計，我們在17個州運作321家後急性照護設施，每日服務逾31,700位病患。我們的歷史性成長主要由我們在收購表現不佳的長期護理專業護理設施，並將其轉型為更高階、更高價值的短期過渡性專業護理設施的專業能力所驅動。我們相信我們的成功在很大程度上來自於我們的本地領導、中央支援的運作模式，透過此模式，我們賦予各設施的本地領導者自主運作的權力，並提供卓越的臨牀品質與優越的病患體驗。我們為獨立運作的設施提供一套完整的科技、支援與後勤服務，使本地領導團隊能更專注於提供高品質的病患照護。我們相信此運作模式為所有醫療保健相關利害關係人帶來價值，包括病患與家屬、轉介醫療提供者、支付者與行政與臨牀人員。

後急性照護生態系統服務需要額外協助恢復急性病狀、疾病或嚴重醫療程序後出院的個體。此生態系統從高階、高成本的設施，如長期急性照護醫院與住院復健設施，至低階、低成本的設施，如輔助生活設施與居家照護。專業護理設施（SNFs）位於此生態系統的中心，並在提供出院後仍需24小時住院服務的病患的費用效益設施照護中扮演關鍵角色。SNFs可提供長期護理與更高價值的短期過渡性照護。專業護理設施產業規模龐大且持續成長，根據美國醫療保險與醫療援助管理服務中心（CMS）預期，產業總支出將從2022年的193.6十億美元增至2031年的283.3十億美元，代表年複合成長率（CAGR）為4.3%。根據CMS報告的設施數量，我們是美國最大的SNF經營者之一。我們主要專注於提供更高價值的短期過渡性照護，並相信我們獨特地處於SNF產業當前基礎趨勢中，並能抓住預期需求的成長部分。

我們相信醫療保健是地方性的，並透過本地領導、中央支援的模式運作，認知到每位病患、設施與社區都是獨特的。為此，我們相信本地領導者及其團隊瞭解其病患、員工與設施的獨特需求與優先事項，並最適合做出臨牀與運作決策，以優化病患的結果與體驗。為此，我們的每個設施均獨立運作，由設施經理及其跨專業團隊，包括醫療主管、護理師、治療師、專門諮詢顧問與運營人員領導。為協助這些本地團隊實現最佳的臨牀與運作潛力，我們為每個設施提供PACS服務的存取，並受PACS商業行為準則與道德規範（於本報告其他部分有說明）及其他多種政策與程序的約束，以確保我們的運作符合適用法律與謹慎商業實踐。PACS服務是一套完整的服務，包括會計、財務、人力資源、薪資、應收與應付款項、法律、合規與風險管理服務，以及一整套強大的科技工具。我們運作於高度管制的產業中，有嚴格的合規義務，這需要強大的合規運作。未能遵守適用法律與規範，可能導致重大支出，並產生合規缺失及其他處罰。PACS服務透過受控的收費與成本報告實務，以及法律、風險管理與合規支援，協助我們履行組織內的合規義務。PACS服務也提供區域專業團隊作為每個設施的資源，包括每個運營區域的區域副總裁（RVP），以及區域臨牀與非臨牀主管與顧問。我們開發PACS服務，作為協助減少行政負擔的資源，使本地領導團隊能專注於做出改善病患照護、福祉與生活品質的決策。
我們相信具備才能的本地領導是我們獨立運作、中央支援設施模式成功的重要關鍵。在設施層面，經理們實際上是首席執行官，並與其他本地執照專業人員共同負責其設施的日常運作。我們致力於招募、培訓與獎勵具備動態的設施經理，並依賴他們與其跨專業團隊

團隊必須實施適當且有效的政策與程序，以產生正面結果。我們支持透過建立優秀團隊來提供卓越照護。我們相信我們的模式能吸引高素質、具創業精神的專業人才，這些人才重視擁有相當程度的自主權、責任感與目標一致的激勵措施。我們為這些專業人才提供領導與產業訓練、指導與運營支援。我們的模式旨在將當地領導者的激勵措施與設施與組織的成功相連結，鼓勵他們專注於設施的長期未來。為創造這種連結，我們已發展出一套管理員薪酬結構，優先考量運營與財務表現，以及照護品質。我們的管理員瞭解，一個表現良好的設施是提供優質照護的結果，並在一個能促進療癒與關懷的環境中，並具備適當人力、供應與設備，以符合患者需求。我們的管理員及其當地團隊對患者結果的專注，驅動了對我們服務的需求，最終可能導致更高的患者人數與利潤。我們也致力於提供向上職業發展的機會，許多我們的管理員是由本公司內部晉升至更高層級責任的職位。我們的 meritocracy 文化與擁有感自豪，已幫助我們留住經驗豐富的設施管理員以及 RVPs，這些 RVPs 在 2025 年 12 月 31 日時平均產業經驗為 12.9 年。

我們的使命以患者在臨牀品質與經驗上的卓越為首要目標。我們相信我們對品質的重視反映在 CMS 品質指標（QM）星級評分、佔用率，以及護理患者天數的專業組合（這指的是 Medicare 與 managed care 患者在 SNFs 接受專業護理服務的天數，佔所有付費來源患者在 SNFs 接受專業護理服務總天數的百分比）。QM 星級評分是為參與 Medicare 或 Medicaid 的 SNFs 所分配的 1 到 5 之間的數字，並根據一組品質報告計畫要求的總分來計算。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年及 2023 年，我們在 Mature 設施（我們定義為在測量日期前超過 36 個月購買的設施）的平均 QM 星級評分分別為 4.4、4.3 和 4.2 星，相較於產業平均為 3.5、3.4 和 3.6 星。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年及 2023 年，我們在 Mature 設施的平均佔用率分別為 95%、94% 和 93%，相較於產業平均為 79%、77% 和 76%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的護理患者天數專業組合為 29%，如 Item 7 所定義的 Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations 所述。

我們歷來主要透過我們嚴謹且平衡的收購策略來成長。我們通常旨在透過識別並收購表現不佳的 custodial care 專注設施，並將其轉型為更高價值的短期過渡照護專注設施，透過投資臨牀團隊與流程，以及升級科技、設備、訓練、人力、美觀以及其他業務方面來實現。PACS Services 提供的資源與指導是快速整合新設施的關鍵，並為當地領導團隊提供有效的科技基礎設施、支援工具與區域支援團隊，使當地領導團隊能專注於運營改善。我們的設施通常會進行最多三年的收購後轉型期。在此期間，我們致力於實施最佳實務，以實現並維持設施的全部潛力。這些實務常導致臨牀品質及其他運營指標的重大改善，包括專業組合、佔用率與付費者合約。我們相信我們收購策略的結果體現在我們在 Mature 設施的高平均 QM 星級評分與佔用率，分別為 4.4 星與 95%，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在 New 設施（我們定義為在測量日期前少於 18 個月購買的設施）的平均 QM 星級評分與佔用率分別為 3.5 星與 81%。

我們所擁有的及租賃的不動產組合戰略性地分佈在 17 個州：阿拉斯加、亞利桑那、加州、科羅拉多、愛達荷、堪薩斯、肯塔基、密蘇裏、蒙大拿、內華達、俄亥俄、俄勒岡、賓州、南卡羅來納、田納西、德州與華盛頓。我們預期可用的收購機會將使我們能進一步擴展在這些 17 個州的業務，並在未來進入新的州。我們認為我們目前的市場具有吸引力，且我們運營的每個州都有其獨特的優勢，例如有利的報銷動態、高進入門檻，或 65 歲以上成年人人口成長，這是我們的主要患者人口統計。我們在進入新市場時通常會尋找類似的特徵。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們租賃了 219 個設施，直接擁有 53 個設施的不動產，並透過第三方管理的合夥關係擁有 49 個設施的部分權益。隨著我們持續成長，我們打算透過現有租賃中的購買選項或優先購買權，以及收購與從零開始建設專用設施，來探索更多的不動產資產購入。

會計年度終了為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司產生總營業收入為 5.3 十億美元，較過去三年的年複合成長率為 30.4%。我們營業收入的相當大一部分來自第三方付款人支付的費用，包括 Medicare 與 Medicaid，這些為我們最大的營業收入來源，並分別佔 2025 年 12 月 31 日會計年度終了之例行營業收入的 33.7% 與 40.5%。會計年度終了為 2024 年 12 月 31 日，本公司
產生總營業收入 4.1 十億美元，且 medicare 與 medicare 佔我們常規營業收入的 33.8% 與 40.4%。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，我們總營運費用為 5.0 十億美元。於相同期間，我們產生淨收入 191.5 百萬美元，以及調整後 EBITDA 505.0 百萬美元。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年，我們總營運費用為 4.0 十億美元，並產生淨收入 55.3 百萬美元，以及調整後 EBITDA 279.5 百萬美元。調整後 EBITDA 為非 GAAP 財務指標。請參閱標題為 "項目 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析—關鍵專業服務指標與非 GAAP 財務指標—非 GAAP 財務指標" 的部分，以瞭解調整後 EBITDA 與最直接可比 GAAP 財務指標的關係。
截至2025年12月31日，我們總長期負債為3.6十億美元。
我們的本地領導、中央支援模式，源於我們相信「醫療是本地化的」，且每位病患、機構與社區皆為獨特。我們的行政人員在決策過程中擁有相當大的自主權，但須遵守公司政策與程序，因為我們相信他們最瞭解其社區與市場的需要。我們的321間後續護理機構，由跨專業團隊獨立運作，並獲得PACS Services強大的行政與諮詢支援。

我們努力讓每間機構由經驗豐富且具備高度資格的行政人員領導，其在實際上擔任「當地總裁」的角色，並與跨專業醫療主任、臨牀人員、專科顧問與運營人員共同合作。除了完整的臨牀團隊，包括認證護理助理（CNAs）、執照實習護士（LPNs）、註冊護士（RNs）、護理主任（DONs）與臨牀主任外，每間機構還擁有當地非臨牀團隊，包括主管、入院專業人員、行銷專業人員與其他業務支援人員，他們共同的目標是為病患提供優質的照護與卓越的服務經驗。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與我們經審計之合併財務報表及相關附註說明一併參考。本報告中部分資訊，包括有關我們業務計畫與策略之資訊，包含風險與不確定性之預測性陳述。您應閱讀標題為「風險因素」及「預測性陳述特別說明」之部分，以瞭解可能導致實際結果與預測性陳述中所述或暗示之結果有重大差異之重要因素。我們的歷史財務表現未必能代表未來之表現。
有關2023年12月31日財務年度與2024年12月31日財務年度之比較，請參閱我們2024年12月31日財務年度之年度報告（Form 10-K）中標題為「第7項 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」之內容，該報告已於2025年11月19日向證券交易委員會（SEC）提交。

我們是一家主要提供高品質專業護理服務之後續護理醫療公司，透過一組獨立運作之設施來提供服務。本公司於2013年成立，根據設施數量而言，我們是美國最大的專業護理服務提供者之一。我們也提供長者照護、輔助生活及獨立生活之選擇，於部分社區中。截至2025年12月31日，我們的設施組合包含17個州之321處後續護理、輔助生活及獨立生活設施，每日服務逾31,700位患者。我們認為我們過去的顯著成長主要來自於我們在收購表現不佳之長期照護專業護理設施，並轉型為高價值短暫過渡照護專業護理設施之專業能力。我們相信我們的成功在很大程度上來自於我們的本地領導、中央支援之運作模式，透過此模式，我們賦予各設施之本地領導者自主運作之權力，並提供優質之臨牀品質與優越之患者體驗。我們為獨立運作之設施提供一套完整的科技、支援與後勤服務，使本地領導團隊能更專注於提供優質照護。我們相信我們的運作模式為所有醫療相關利害關係人創造價值，包括患者與家屬、轉介醫療人員、付款方及管理與臨牀人員。

我們旨在透過識別並收購表現不佳之長期照護設施，並轉型為高價值短暫過渡照護設施，以創造價值。我們透過投資臨牀團隊與流程，並升級科技、設備、訓練、人力、美觀及其他業務方面，來實現此目標。我們相信PACS Services所提供的資源與指導對新設施之快速整合至關重要，並為本地領導團隊提供有效的科技基礎設施、支援工具及區域支援團隊，使本地領導團隊能專注於運作改善。我們的設施通常會進行最多三年之收購後過渡期。在此期間，我們致力於落實最佳實務，以實現並維持設施之潛力。這些實務常導致臨牀品質及其他運作指標，包括專業護理組合、入住率及付款方合約之顯著改善。我們相信我們收購策略的結果，透過我們截至2025年12月31日之成熟設施平均QM Star評分為4.4，入住率為95%來體現。截至2025年12月31日，新設施之平均QM Star評分為3.5，入住率為81%。

如先前於我們2024年12月31日財務年度之年度報告（Form 10-K）中所披露，該報告已於2025年11月19日向證券交易委員會（SEC）提交，我們發現我們財務報告內部控制之重大弱點，即我們未設計並維護足夠的程序，以識別、評估並與適當層級組織溝通相關風險，包括透過熱線程序收到之潛在合規問題，以及我們未設計並維護足夠的控制，以根據財務會計標準委員會（FASB）會計準則主題606（與客戶之合約收入）適當地確認新服務之收入。
此外，在準備我們2025年12月31日財務年度之合併財務報表時，我們的管理層發現內部控制之控制缺陷，這些缺陷個別或合計而言，構成我們財務報告內部控制之重大弱點。管理層發現的重大弱點為：我們未設計並維護有效的控制，以處理用於確定常規收入之基礎資料之完整性和準確性。我們也未設計控制，以及時評估可能對收入確認之變動考量估計產生重大影響之運作趨勢。
此外，我們的首席執行官與臨時首席財務官已結論，由於重大弱點，我們的揭露控制與程序在證券交易法規13a-15(e)及15(d)-15(e)之定義下，截至2025年12月31日並未有效運作。管理層致力於維持強大的內部控制環境。為回應上述發現的重大弱點，管理層在審計委員會監督下，已採取全面措施以解決上述重大弱點。有關重大弱點及我們的解決步驟之更多資訊，請參閱「第二部分，第9A項 控制與程序」。
考慮上述重大弱點，管理層已執行額外分析及其他程序，以確保我們之合併財務報表依美國通用會計準則（U.S. GAAP）編製。因此，管理層相信本年度報告（Form 10-K）中所包含之合併財務報表，就其重大方面而言，真實且恰當地反映我們截至財務報表所列期間之財務狀況、營運成果及現金流，依美國通用會計準則（U.S. GAAP）編製。
我們使用以下關鍵技能服務指標及非GAAP財務指標，以協助我們評估業務、識別影響財務表現的趨勢，並做出戰略決策。
我們監測以下關鍵技能服務指標，涵蓋所有設施，並依成熟設施、擴充設施及新設設施分類。成熟設施定義為購入時間超過36個月前的設施。擴充設施定義為購入時間在18至36個月前的設施。新設設施定義為購入或新建時間少於18個月前的設施。
•技能照護服務收入 — 技能照護服務收入反映來自所有技能照護設施患者的患者及住民服務收入中，扣除來自我們輔助及獨立生活服務的收入部分。
•技能組成 — 我們依付款方衡量收入與護理患者天數。醫療保險及管理照護患者，我們稱為高需求患者，通常需要較高水平的技能照護服務。因此，醫療保險及管理照護的補償率通常高於其他付款方。在大多數州，醫療救助的補償率通常是所有付款方中最低的。付款方組成的變化會顯著影響我們的收入與利潤。為監測此表現，我們評估兩種不同的技能組成指標：

◦技能組成按收入 — 技能組成按收入代表來自高需求醫療保險及管理照護患者的收入比例。常規收入指的是透過合約每日費用收取的技能照護服務收入。在合約外提供的服務則單獨記錄為輔助收入，包括醫療保險Part B治療服務，並非常規收入。治療及其他輔助治療是否包含在合約每日費用中，視付款方來源及合約而定。計算技能組成的收入與合約協議的金額或費用有關，排除根據收入確認標準，財務會計標準委員會（FASB）會計準則編碼（ASC）主題606，與客戶的合約收入（ASC 606）中變動考量的估計值。
◦技能組成按護理患者天數 — 技能組成按護理患者天數代表高需求醫療保險及管理照護患者在技能照護設施中接受技能照護服務的天數，佔所有付款方來源患者在技能照護設施中接受技能照護服務總天數的百分比。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關的風險
對護理師、護理助理及其他專業人員的競爭增加，或出現短缺，可能會提高我們的僱用及勞動成本，並使我們面臨財務處罰的風險。
若我們無法吸引病人及住民，並有效與其他醫療服務提供者競爭，我們的營業收入與獲利能力可能會下降，並可能產生虧損。
我們的業務可能受到人工智慧科技相關規範框架持續演進的影響。
我們高度依賴資訊科技，若該科技發生故障、不足或中斷，可能會影響我們有效運作業務的能力。
我們可能無法成功將取得的設施與不動產整合至我們的營運中，且可能無法實現我們預期的設施取得效益。
我們可能在完成符合我們成長策略的合夥關係時遇到困難。
若我們無法達成或維持來自 CMS 或從事類似評分活動的私人機構的競爭性照護品質評分，我們的業務可能會受到負面影響。

paragraphs: 本公司業務涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列各項風險因素，以及本報告與本公司其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交的申報文件中所載的其他資訊。根據目前本公司所知的資訊，我們認為下列資訊識別出對本公司最重要的風險因素。此外，過去的財務表現未必是未來表現的可靠指標，歷史趨勢也不應用來預測未來期間的結果或趨勢。
若下列風險與不確定性發展成為實際事件或情況，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。您應仔細閱讀下列風險因素，並與本公司合併/整體財務報表及其相關附註，以及本報告與本公司其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交的申報文件中所載的其他資訊一併審閱。本報告包含前瞻性陳述，其中包含風險與不確定性。
本公司依賴第三方付費者之補償，若本公司營收、財務狀況及營運成果受到我們設施中患者急性程度組成的變化，以及付費者組成與付款方式的變化，以及第三方付費者的新成本控制措施的影響，將可能受到負面影響。

本公司營收受到我們營運子公司中患者需要高度專業護理與復健照護比例的影響，我們稱這些患者為高急性程度患者或專業護理患者，並受到我們付款來源組成的影響。我們吸引的患者急性程度水平的變化，以及我們在醫療補助（Medicaid）、醫療保險（Medicare）、私人付費者與管理式醫療公司之間的付費者組成，會顯著影響我們的營收。影響醫療補助（Medicaid）資金與可得性的聯邦法規變動，包括《OBBBA》的通過，可能會對本公司業務與我們獨立子公司之營運產生重大影響。由於高急性程度患者需要更多專業護理服務與較高水平的照護，我們通常會為照顧這些患者收取較高的補償金率。低急性程度患者，通常是醫療補助（Medicaid）受益者，通常需要較少專業護理服務，因此我們通常會為照顧這些患者收取較低的補償金率，有時甚至低於我們照顧這些患者的成本。為照顧專業護理患者所提供的補償金率較有可能達到或超過照顧這些患者的成本，從而使機構財務上可持續。由於我們為照顧患者所收取的補償金率通常為預先確定，若我們的勞動力或其他營運成本相對於我們為提供服務所收取的補償金率增加過度，特別是在醫療補助（Medicaid）患者的情況下，我們通常無法從付費者處收回增加的成本，除非且直到補償金率調整，而即使如此，補償金率也可能不會在及時 manner 調整，且通常僅在事前 basis 調整。因此，若我們無法維持高急性程度患者的比例，或若我們營運子公司中接受醫療補助（Medicaid）補償的患者比例出現顯著增加，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。

主要保險公司與管理式醫療公司為降低其成本與支付給提供者的金額，所採取的行動可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。這些行動包括與醫療提供者簽訂合同以以折扣價格取得服務。我們認為此趨勢將持續，可能會限制對醫療服務的補償金額。若我們從中獲得重大支付的保險公司或管理式醫療公司減少他們為服務所支付的金額，而我們不願接受這些減少，我們可能在選擇不與這些保險公司續約時失去患者。此外，一些付費者已利用美國的「無驚訝法案」或類似的州立法作為重新協商提供者與機構補償金率的手段，導致這些提供者與/或機構對付費者提起訴訟，這也可能對本公司產生不利影響。此外，持續的不利經濟情況可能影響加入管理式醫療計劃的患者數量與管理式醫療公司的盈利能力，這可能會導致支付金額減少。
我們可能無法完全獲得所有設施透過合併計費或包裝付款所計費服務的補償，這可能會對我們的營收、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
